fn.ABS: Returns the absolute value of a number.
fn.ACOS: Returns the arccosine of a number, in radians.
fn.ADDRESS: Builds a cell address as text from a row and column number.
fn.AGGREGATE: Calculates a total (sum, average, …) and can ignore errors and hidden rows.
fn.AND: TRUE if all arguments are TRUE.
fn.ASIN: Returns the arcsine of a number, in radians.
fn.ATAN: Returns the arctangent of a number, in radians.
fn.ATAN2: Returns the arctangent of x and y coordinates, in radians.
fn.AVEDEV: Average absolute deviation of the data from their mean.
fn.AVERAGE: Returns the average of the arguments.
fn.AVERAGEA: Average, counting text as 0 and TRUE as 1.
fn.AVERAGEIF: Average of the cells that meet a condition.
fn.AVERAGEIFS: Average of the cells that meet several conditions.
fn.BYCOL: Applies a LAMBDA to each column and returns the results as an array.
fn.BYROW: Applies a LAMBDA to each row and returns the results as an array.
fn.CEILING: Rounds a number up to a multiple of significance.
fn.CHAR: Returns the character for a character code.
fn.CHOOSE: Picks a value from a list by its index.
fn.CHOOSECOLS: Returns the given columns of an array.
fn.CHOOSEROWS: Returns the given rows of an array.
fn.CODE: Returns the code of the first character.
fn.COLUMN: Returns the column number of a reference.
fn.COLUMNS: Returns the number of columns in an array or range.
fn.CONVERT: Converts a number to another unit.
fn.CORREL: Returns the correlation coefficient of two data sets.
fn.COS: Returns the cosine of an angle in radians.
fn.COSH: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of a number.
fn.COUNT: Counts the cells that contain numbers.
fn.COUNTA: Counts the cells that are not empty.
fn.COUNTBLANK: Counts the empty cells in a range.
fn.COUNTIF: Counts the cells that meet a condition.
fn.COUNTIFS: Counts the cells that meet several conditions.
fn.COVAR: Returns the covariance of two data sets (population).
fn.DATE: Builds a date from year, month and day.
fn.DATEDIF: Counts days, months or years between two dates.
fn.DATEVALUE: Converts a date in text form to a date serial number.
fn.DAY: Returns the day of the month (1–31).
fn.DAYS: Returns the number of days between two dates.
fn.DEVSQ: Sum of squared deviations from the mean.
fn.DROP: Removes rows or columns from the start or end of an array.
fn.EDATE: Date a number of months before or after a start date.
fn.EOMONTH: Last day of the month, a number of months away.
fn.EXACT: TRUE if two texts are exactly the same (case-sensitive).
fn.EXP: Returns e raised to the power of a number.
fn.EXPAND: Expands an array to the given number of rows and columns.
fn.FILTER: Filters a range by a condition.
fn.FIND: Finds text within text (case-sensitive) and returns its position.
fn.FLOOR: Rounds a number down to a multiple of significance.
fn.FORMULATEXT: Returns the formula of a cell as text.
fn.FREQUENCY: Counts how often values fall into bins.
fn.FV: Future value of an investment with fixed payments and rate.
fn.HLOOKUP: Looks in the top row and returns a value from a row below.
fn.HYPERLINK: Creates a link to a document or website.
fn.IF: Returns one value if the condition is TRUE and another if it is FALSE.
fn.IFERROR: Returns your own value if the formula returns an error.
fn.IFNA: Returns your own value if the formula returns #N/A.
fn.IFS: Tests conditions in order and returns the value of the first TRUE one.
fn.INDEX: Returns a value at a row and column number in a range.
fn.INDIRECT: Returns the reference given as text.
fn.INTERCEPT: Point where the regression line crosses the y axis.
fn.ISBLANK: TRUE if the cell is empty.
fn.ISEVEN: TRUE if the number is even.
fn.ISLOGICAL: TRUE if the value is TRUE or FALSE.
fn.ISNUMBER: TRUE if the value is a number.
fn.ISODD: TRUE if the number is odd.
fn.ISOWEEKNUM: Returns the ISO week number of a date.
fn.ISTEXT: TRUE if the value is text.
fn.KURT: Returns the kurtosis of a data set.
fn.LEFT: Returns the first characters of a text.
fn.LEN: Returns the number of characters in a text.
fn.LET: Names intermediate results inside a formula.
fn.LINEST: Statistics of a linear trend (least squares).
fn.LOG: Returns the logarithm to a base.
fn.LOOKUP: Looks up a value in one row or column.
fn.MAKEARRAY: Builds an array by applying a LAMBDA to each cell.
fn.MAP: Applies a LAMBDA to each value of arrays.
fn.MATCH: Returns the position of a value in a range.
fn.MAXA: Largest value, counting text as 0 and TRUE as 1.
fn.MAXIFS: Largest value in cells that meet conditions.
fn.MID: Returns characters from the middle of a text.
fn.MINA: Smallest value, counting text as 0 and TRUE as 1.
fn.MINIFS: Smallest value in cells that meet conditions.
fn.N: Converts a value to a number.
fn.NETWORKDAYS: Counts the working days between two dates.
fn.NETWORKDAYS.INTL: Counts working days with a custom weekend.
fn.NOW: Returns the current date and time.
fn.NPER: Number of periods of an investment.
fn.NPV: Net present value of future payments.
fn.NUMBERVALUE: Converts text to a number with your own separators.
fn.OFFSET: Returns a reference shifted from a cell.
fn.OR: TRUE if at least one argument is TRUE.
fn.POWER: Raises a number to a power.
fn.PROPER: Capitalises the first letter of each word.
fn.QUOTIENT: Returns the integer part of a division.
fn.RANK: Returns the rank of a number in a list.
fn.RANK.EQ: Returns the rank of a number in a list.
fn.REDUCE: Reduces an array to one value with a LAMBDA.
fn.REPLACE: Replaces characters at a position in a text.
fn.REPT: Repeats a text a number of times.
fn.RIGHT: Returns the last characters of a text.
fn.ROUND: Rounds a number to a number of decimals.
fn.ROUNDUP: Rounds a number away from zero.
fn.ROW: Returns the row number of a reference.
fn.ROWS: Returns the number of rows in an array or range.
fn.SCAN: Applies a LAMBDA cumulatively and returns each step.
fn.SEARCH: Finds text within text (not case-sensitive) and returns its position.
fn.SEQUENCE: Creates a sequence of consecutive numbers.
fn.SIGN: Returns the sign of a number: 1, 0 or -1.
fn.SIN: Returns the sine of an angle in radians.
fn.SINH: Returns the hyperbolic sine of a number.
fn.SKEW: Returns the skewness of a distribution.
fn.SORTBY: Sorts a range by the values of another range.
fn.STDEVA: Standard deviation of a sample, including text and logical values.
fn.SUBSTITUTE: Replaces old text with new text.
fn.SUBTOTAL: Subtotal that can skip hidden rows.
fn.SUMIF: Adds the cells that meet a condition.
fn.SUMIFS: Adds the cells that meet several conditions.
fn.SUMPRODUCT: Sum of the products of matching elements.
fn.SWITCH: Compares an expression with values and returns the matching result.
fn.T: Returns text; other values as empty text.
fn.TAKE: Returns rows or columns from the start or end of an array.
fn.TAN: Returns the tangent of an angle in radians.
fn.TANH: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of a number.
fn.TEXT: Turns a value into text using a number format.
fn.TEXTAFTER: Returns the text after a delimiter.
fn.TEXTBEFORE: Returns the text before a delimiter.
fn.TEXTSPLIT: Splits text into columns and rows.
fn.TIME: Builds a time from hour, minute and second.
fn.TIMEVALUE: Converts a time in text form to a number.
fn.TOCOL: Turns an array into a single column.
fn.TOROW: Turns an array into a single row.
fn.TRUNC: Truncates a number to an integer or a number of decimals.
fn.UNIQUE: Returns the unique values of a range.
fn.VLOOKUP: Looks in the first column and returns a value from a column next to it.
fn.VSTACK: Stacks arrays on top of each other.
fn.WEEKDAY: Returns the day of the week as a number.
fn.WEEKNUM: Returns the week number in the year.
fn.WORKDAY: Date a number of working days away.
fn.WORKDAY.INTL: Date a number of working days away, with a custom weekend.
fn.WRAPCOLS: Wraps a row or column into columns.
fn.WRAPROWS: Wraps a row or column into rows.
fn.XLOOKUP: Looks up a value and returns the matching result, in any direction.
fn.XMATCH: Returns the position of a value, with more search options.
fn.XOR: TRUE if an odd number of arguments are TRUE.
fn.YEAR: Returns the year of a date.
fn.YEARFRAC: Fraction of the year between two dates.

arg.a: TRUE or omitted for A1 style, FALSE for R1C1 style.
arg.abs_num: Reference type: 1 absolute, 2 absolute row, 3 absolute column, 4 relative.
arg.average_range: Cells to average; omitted: the range itself.
arg.basis: Day count: 0 US 30/360, 1 actual, 2 actual/360, 3 actual/365, 4 European 30/360.
arg.by_col: TRUE to work by column instead of by row.
arg.calculation: The formula that returns the result.
arg.col_delimiter: Text to split into columns at.
arg.col_index_num: Column number in the table to return the value from.
arg.const: TRUE or omitted: calculate the intercept; FALSE: through zero.
arg.cumulative: TRUE for the cumulative distribution, FALSE for the density.
arg.exactly_once: TRUE to return only values that occur exactly once.
arg.format_text: Number format as text, for example "0.00".
arg.function_num: Number of the function, for example 9 for sum.
arg.ignore: What to skip: 0 nothing, 1 blanks, 2 errors, 3 both.
arg.include: Condition per row or column (TRUE to keep).
arg.k: Position in the ranking, or fraction.
arg.logical_test: Condition that gives TRUE or FALSE.
arg.m: Step by which the power increases.
arg.match_end: TRUE to treat the end of the text as a delimiter.
arg.match_mode: How to match: exact, approximate or with wildcards.
arg.match_type: 1 less than or equal, 0 exact, -1 greater than or equal.
arg.max_range: Cells to take the maximum of.
arg.min_range: Cells to take the minimum of.
arg.months: Number of months; negative for earlier.
arg.name: Name for an intermediate result.
arg.number: A number or a reference to a number.
arg.options: What to ignore, for example 6 for errors.
arg.percent: Share of the data to exclude.
arg.range_lookup: FALSE for exact; TRUE or omitted for approximate.
arg.result_vector: Row or column with the results.
arg.return_array: Range with the values to return.
arg.row_delimiter: Text to split into rows at.
arg.row_index_num: Row number in the table to return the value from.
arg.search_mode: Search direction: 1 from the top, -1 from the bottom.
arg.sort_index: Column or row to sort by.
arg.text: A text or a reference to text.
arg.type: 0 payment at the end, 1 at the start of the period.
arg.value_if_false: Result if the condition is FALSE.
arg.value_if_true: Result if the condition is TRUE.
arg.weekend: Which days are the weekend, for example 1 for Sat and Sun.
arg.wrap_count: Number of values per row or column.
